summary.text: 木 means “tree” or “wood.” It began as a drawing of a whole tree, with branches spreading above and roots below. The modern strokes retain that outline in a more regular form; the character is best understood as one picture.

formation.text: A whole-tree pictograph, without a separate sound component.

components.text: The branching top and spreading roots belong to a single tree outline. They are parts of the drawing, not independently meaningful characters.

history.text: An older analysis splits off the upper part as 屮, a plant shoot. That division mistakes a similar shape for a separate component: the early tree drawing is complete in itself.
